title: oncall-handoff-notes-ryan-patel
content:
Shift: Mar 1 22:00 - Mar 2 06:00 (UTC)
Owner: Ryan Patel (eng-sre)
Handoff summary (quick):
- Quiet shift overall. Two alerts: high-queue-length on text-generation-prod (short spike) and a single worker OOM on dedicated-pool-3. Both auto-recovered with existing policies; brief manual follow-up applied for the OOM.
- No ongoing Sev. All postmortem tracking started for the OOM (see JIRA-INC-4123).

Outstanding items for next oncall:
- Follow up with infra team about dedicated-pool-3 memory anomaly (PR referenced below). I opened a short ticket to cap per-container memory to 36GB as a short-term mitigation.
- Keep an eye on prefix-cache hit-rate for chat endpoints — small drop seen around 02:10 UTC (could be cache eviction due to recent model rollout).
- Maya to verify that we rolled back model-variant v2.3.1 for low-latency customers (tagged rollback executed at 02:40 UTC).

Incidents (details):
1) OOM on dedicated-pool-3 (02:05 UTC)
  - Symptom: single worker exited with oom-kill, pod restarted and rejoined. No customer-facing errors observed.
  - Immediate action: cordoned node, restarted pod, adjusted container memory request (from 40Gi -> 38Gi) pending infra PR to implement pod-level limit.
  - Temp mitigation: restarted affected replica 3x to warm KV cache and reduce cold-start latency.
  - Follow-ups: deeper memory profiling of model-serving container; check recent model weights (v2.3.1) loaded at 01:45 UTC. Jira: JIRA-INC-4123. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284

2) High queue length alert on text-generation-prod (01:55 UTC)
  - Symptom: latency was within SLO but queue length exceeded threshold for ~3m. Caused by a burst of small requests from partner test. Auto-scaler scaled up 2 nodes; queues drained. No action required.
  - Note: consider shorter autoscaler cool-down or pre-warming rules for partner tenants.

Temporary procedures / runbook drafts (quick reference)
- If a pod OOMs repeatedly (>3 times in 15m):
  1) Check pod logs (/var/log/pods/<pod>) for oom messages and last stack trace.
  2) Cordone node and restart the pod on different node (kubectl cordon/drain).
  3) Increase memory request by 2Gi and restart if immediate cause unclear.
  4) Open (or link to) a JIRA ticket with logs, heap/profile snapshot, and model version. Tag eng-serving-runtime and infra.
  5) If customer impact, escalate to oncall-2 and notify #sre-oncall and #prod-ops.

- If queue-length alert fires but latency OK:
  1) Check autoscaler events (kubectl get hpa/ksa events) and scale activity.
  2) Look for traffic spikes in logs (filter by tenant-id).
  3) If bursty partner traffic, reach out via partner slack or oncall contact; consider adding short-term rate-limits.

- If RPC gateway errors 5xx across region:
  1) Check gateway logs and envoy stats.
  2) Confirm backend pool health (kubectl get pods -n prod -l app=gateway).
  3) Rollback recent gateway config if a config push happened in last 15m (see config-manager history).

Useful commands (quick copy-paste)
- kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=model-server -o wide
- kubectl -n prod logs <pod> -c model-server --tail=500
- kubectl -n prod describe pod <pod>
- kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
- kubectl -n infra get hpa text-gen-autoscaler -o yaml

Recent changes to be aware of
- 2026-03-01 01:30 UTC: Model variant v2.3.1 deployed to a subset of low-latency tenants (rollout paused at 02:20 due to latency regression reports).
- 2026-02-28 17:00 UTC: infra PR #1284 applied (node memory tuning). See PR for details — might be related to OOMs.

Contacts / escalation
- Oncall-2: Maya Singh (pager)
- Infra lead: Diego Alvarez (pager)
- Eng-serving-runtime: @eng-runtime-slack (channel)
- PagerDuty: PD schedule "sre-oncall"

Notes & loose thoughts (scratchpad)
- Possible root cause for OOM: model variant v2.3.1 loads slightly larger kv/cache object — check tokenizer cache retention settings.
- Consider adding a canary-only flag (runtime) to limit memory-heavy features during rollout.
- Metrics to add: per-model peak-RSS histogram, pod-level ephemeral cache usage (gauge).
- Clean up: When PR-1284 is merged into prod, validate that memoryRequest vs memoryLimit are aligned across node types.

Todo (for next shift or follow-up)
- Maya: confirm rollback/variant state for low-latency tenants (blocked?)
- Me: run mem-profiling job on dedicated-pool-3 (script in infra/tools/mem-profiler)
- Diego: review infra PR and suggest permanent pod-level limit
- Create perf-test that imitates partner burst pattern to reproduce queue spike locally

Attachments / refs
- infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284
- JIRA: JIRA-INC-4123 (oom on dedicated-pool-3)
- Confluence runbook index: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/OPS-Runbook-Index

Final note: most things auto-healed, but OOM is the only thing that needs follow-up. If you see repeated OOMs, escalate early — we've had subtle model changes that increase resident set.

-- Ryan
(leave quick message in #sre-oncall if you take over)
